prompt:
Platform-automation ticket. We are moving a day-2 deployment action out of a brittle shell script and into VCF Automation 9.1, the successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation. The script currently guesses a deployment UUID and treats the action submission response as completion. Implement the replacement as the single production source file VcfAutomationClient.java, using only the JDK (java.net.http is available; no Maven and no external jars). TestMain.java is the acceptance harness.

Before changing code, research the current official VCF Automation xAPIs reference on developer.broadcom.com for Get Deployments, Submit Deployment Action Request, and Get Request. These VCF Automation operations do not have a published specification in the Apache-2.0 vmware/vcf-api-specs repository, so docs/contract.json is explicitly a reference-documentation-derived contract, not a published specification. Its provenance is recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Both files are protected. If the current official reference disagrees with the pinned contract, mention the discrepancy in your final summary and do not edit the fixtures. Cite the exact official pages you read.

Implement this surface:

- VcfAutomationClient(String baseUrl, String bearerToken, java.time.Duration pollInterval).
- VcfAutomationClient.OperationResult runDeploymentAction(String deploymentName, String actionId, java.util.Map<String,Object> inputs, String reason). OperationResult exposes deploymentId(), requestId(), and status().

runDeploymentAction must perform the contract's whole asynchronous lifecycle. Look up the deployment with the exact-name collection query and use the id from the matching response object; an empty lookup is an error and must not submit anything. Submit the action body to that returned deployment id, take the request id from the submission response, and immediately poll Get Request with that returned request id until the response reaches one of the contract's terminal states. Do not treat the submission acknowledgement or an intermediate status as completion. Return every terminal state, including failure states, in OperationResult. Identifiers used in later paths must come from this invocation's preceding response, never from a constant, a name transformed into an id, or a prior invocation.

Every request sends Accept: application/json and Bearer authorization; requests with a body also send Content-Type: application/json. Preserve the actionId, inputs, and reason in the JSON body. Require the documented 200 success status and report HTTP or malformed-response failures clearly. If interrupted while waiting, restore the thread interrupt flag and fail the operation.

Acceptance is `java TestMain.java`. It runs only a loopback mock pinned to the three operations in docs/contract.json and reads that mock's request log to verify lookup and request-id provenance as well as polling. No live VMware endpoint or real credential is used. TestMain.java and everything under docs/ are protected; do not modify them.

research.interface: VCF Automation Deployment API (developer.broadcom.com xAPIs reference)

official_sources.title: Get Deployments | VM Apps Org - Deployment
official_sources.used_for: GET /deployment/api/deployments; exact name query; paginated PageDeployment content with deployment id and name

official_sources.title: Submit Deployment Action Request | VM Apps Org - Deployment
official_sources.used_for: POST /deployment/api/deployments/{deploymentId}/requests; ResourceActionRequest body; 200 Request response containing request id and status

official_sources.title: Get Request | VM Apps Org - Deployment
official_sources.used_for: GET /deployment/api/requests/{requestId}; 200 Request response and documented request status values

research.language_rationale: A single JDK client is the integration artifact requested by the JVM automation service; java.net.http provides the documented bearer-authenticated JSON REST calls without an SDK or third-party dependency.
